text: Understanding Git branching is an important skill for modern software development. In a typical version control workflow, developers create separate feature branches to work on new ideas without affecting the main code. Once the work is finished, these branches are merged back into the main project. Teams often use pull requests so that other developers can review the changes before merging. This keeps the code clean and reduces mistakes. Branching also allows several people to work on different tasks at the same time. By following a clear workflow, teams can collaborate more easily and keep their projects organised and safe.
